newsitem.title: FRANCE: Parc Asterix draws fewer visitors in 1996 season.
newsitem.headline: Parc Asterix draws fewer visitors in 1996 season.

text.p: France's Parc Asterix, the theme park based on Gaullic cartoon character Asterix, drew 1.7 million visitors during the 1996 season which ended on Sunday, down slightly from 1.8 million in its peak 1995 season.

The company, which plans a listing on the Paris bourse later in the year, said turnover totalled 300 million francs, excluding taxes, level with 1995 revenue, as spending per visitor rose 3.5 percent to 187.30 francs.
It said in a statement that it expected to be profitable for a third consecutive year. It earned 32 million francs in 1995.
Parc Asterix is 27 percent owned by Generale des Eaux, 24 percent owned by Accor and 19 percent owned by Barclays Plc.
The theme park, which will reopen on April 5, 1997, drew 1.6 million visitors in 1994 and 1.2 million in 1993.
In contrast, Euro Disney's larger Disneyland Paris theme park attracted 10.7 million visitors in its 1994/95 year ended last September 30. Disneyland Paris is open year-round.
